question: Which edition of International Conference on 'Arbitrating Indo-UK Commercial Disputes' was organised by the Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA)during the London International Disputes Week (LIDW) in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd Edition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **3rd edition** of the International Conference on 'Arbitrating Indo-UK Commercial Disputes' was organized by the **Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA)** during the **London International Disputes Week (LIDW)** in **June 2025**.
 
• The conference aimed to strengthen **India-UK arbitration relations**, focusing on resolving commercial disputes involving businesses from both nations.
 
• The event provided a platform for legal professionals, arbitrators, and business leaders to discuss the **challenges and developments** in arbitration practices between the two countries.
 
• The Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA) is a premier arbitration body in India, established to promote **alternative dispute resolution mechanisms** and ensure efficient resolution of disputes.
 
• London International Disputes Week (LIDW) is an annual event that gathers professionals from across the globe to focus on **dispute resolution developments**, including arbitration and mediation practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA):**

 
 
• Established in **1965**, ICA operates under the aegis of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (**FICCI**).
 
• It is responsible for promoting **arbitration** as a means of alternative dispute resolution (ADR) in India.
 
• ICA organizes **conferences, training programs, and seminars** to educate professionals about arbitration and ADR mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **London International Disputes Week (LIDW):**
 
 
• LIDW is held annually in London, UK, with participation from global legal and arbitration professionals.
 
• The event focuses on **cross-border disputes**, arbitration practices, and innovations in dispute resolution.
 
• It encourages collaboration between nations to improve arbitration frameworks and practices.
 
 
 
• **India-UK Commercial Relations:**
 
 
• The UK is one of India's **leading trade partners**, with bilateral trade valued at billions of dollars annually.
 
• Arbitration plays a critical role in resolving disputes arising from business transactions and contractual disagreements between entities in both countries.
 
• Strengthening arbitration mechanisms can improve **business confidence** and promote smoother trade relations.
 
 
 
• **Arbitration Practices:**
 
 
• Arbitration is a widely recognized and utilized method for resolving disputes outside of traditional court systems.
 
• It involves appointing neutral arbitrators who deliver legally binding decisions based on evidence and arguments presented by parties.
 
• India has adopted the **Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996**, which aligns with international standards like the **UNCITRAL Model Law**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996:**

 
 
• This Act governs arbitration proceedings in India and incorporates provisions for **domestic and international arbitration**.
 
• It aims to reduce the burden on Indian courts by encouraging **alternative dispute resolution mechanisms**.
 
 
 
• **UNCITRAL Model Law:**
 
 
• The **United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) Model Law** serves as a framework for countries to establish or reform their arbitration laws.
 
• India's Arbitration Act aligns with the **UNCITRAL standards**, ensuring international acceptance of Indian arbitration practices.
 
 
 
• **Cross-Border Arbitration:**
 
 
• Cross-border arbitration resolves disputes involving parties from different nations.
 
• It emphasizes neutrality, efficiency, and enforceability of awards under treaties like the **New York Convention**.
